title: Animal records
text: Humans are not the only record holders. The animal world is full of champions, and some of their records are amazing.
The blue whale is the largest animal that has ever lived. It is bigger than any dinosaur. Its heart is as big as a small car, and its baby drinks hundreds of liters of milk every day.

The cheetah is the fastest land animal. It can run at more than one hundred kilometers per hour, but only for a few seconds. The peregrine falcon is even faster: when it dives from the sky, it reaches more than three hundred kilometers per hour.
The oldest land animal alive is Jonathan, a giant tortoise. He lives on the island of Saint Helena and he was born in about 1832. He is older than cars, planes and telephones!
Some records are strange. The smallest frog in the world is smaller than a pea. And the loudest animal is the sperm whale: its clicks are louder than a rocket.
q: What is the largest animal that has ever lived?
How big is the heart of the blue whale?
As big as a small car
Which is the fastest land animal?
When does the falcon reach more than three hundred kilometers per hour?
When it dives from the sky

grammar.title: Grammar: superlatives
grammar.rule: To say that something is number one, use the + adjective + -est. With long adjectives use the most + adjective.
items: The cheetah is the ___ land animal.
The blue whale is the ___ animal.
Jonathan is the ___ land animal alive.
This is the ___ record of all.
The sperm whale is the ___ animal.

es.title: Récords de animales
es.grammar: Gramática: los superlativos, para decir que algo es el número uno: the + adjetivo + -est. Con adjetivos largos: the most + adjetivo.
